note: Audit-debt ratchet for docs/architecture/distributed-execution-threat-controls.json, read by scripts/check-threat-control-audit-debt.mjs (required `policy` job). WHY IT EXISTS: before W20 the foundation checker validated the SHAPE of deliveryStatus and imposed no cap, deadline or count on `unaudited`, and scripts/check-finding-ownership.mjs globs only docs/replatform/epics/*/findings.md so this register was structurally invisible to the ownership census. Twenty-eight Critical/High controls could therefore sit unaudited forever with policy green, and one of them (DE-11) sat `unaudited` while a committed hand audit of that same crossing concluded all four of its controls were absent. This file carries the pinned numbers; the guard carries the rules. AN ABSENT FILE IS A FAIL (fail-closed), not an empty allow-list.

ceilings.$comment: The number of Critical/High crossings that may carry deliveryStatus `unaudited`. A CEILING, never a target: it may be lowered by auditing a crossing, and lowering it is the ONLY edit this guard accepts in that direction. Raising it, or adding a new unaudited Critical/High row above it, is refused. ★ DO NOT READ THIS AS HEALTH. 16 unaudited Criticals and Highs is the honest measured state, and the ratchet's job is to stop it growing, not to imply it is acceptable.

auditedFloor.$comment: Crossings that HAVE been audited. Each must never return to `unaudited` — that would discard a recorded measurement, which is the one direction this vocabulary must not travel. DE-02 and DE-08 were audited by W4U2; the twelve `partial` rows by W20.

deliveredFloor.$comment: Crossings recorded `delivered` on a measurement. Each must STILL be `delivered`. This is the anti-regression arm: a delivered row silently dropping back to `unaudited` (or to `partial`) is a loss of established fact and reds here. Pinning the SET rather than a count means the guard names which row regressed.

ownerTicketDeferrals.$comment: A crossing that is not `delivered` must name at least one ownerTicket with a file on disk, so its exit route terminates somewhere. Exactly one crossing cannot satisfy that today and it is declared here rather than left invisible — the `unowned`-with-reason pattern this repo already uses for release tests. NOTE the deliberately narrower rule: the guard requires ONE on-disk owner ticket, not that every named ticket exists. Twenty-four of thirty rows also charter their exit to an unwritten REL ticket (REL-001/002/005, zero files each); that debt is declared separately and already in docs/architecture/distributed-execution-release-tests.json, and enforcing it here would red the tree without adding a fact the repo does not already record.

DE-12.reason: ALL THREE ownerTickets — SVC-002, SVC-003, SVC-005 — have zero files on disk, and so does the releaseTest REL-002 and the D4 lane the row's verificationLane names. DE-12 is the only crossing in the register with no on-disk owner ticket at all, i.e. its audit route terminates nowhere at BOTH ends. This is not an oversight to be papered over: the crossing's control (`desired-state reconciler, generation, active fence`) is two-thirds unbuilt, its one shipped part is production-unreachable, and the only authored SVC ticket disclaims it in writing (docs/replatform/epics/E9-service-agents/tickets/SVC-001-terrain.md:216-218). Measured absences are recorded in the crossing's deliveryEvidence and owned by findings E0-F010 and E0-F011. REMOVE THIS ENTRY the moment any of SVC-002/003/005 gets a file — the guard reds on a stale deferral, so it is self-cleaning.
